r1-handoff.finding:
FAIL, BLOCKING on FINDING A. Both Commander findings independently reproduced by running
the code myself, not taken on trust. Ruling on each below, then the four "Also verify" items,
all of which hold up.

=== FINDING A: CONFIRMED, BLOCKING ===

Reproduced directly (not from the diff alone): `render.is_test_module` and `checks.is_test_module`
both return True for `scripts.tests.helpers` and `pkg.sub.tests.foo` -- neither has `tests` as its
FIRST dotted segment, so under the page's own stated rule ("a top-level tests package") both
should classify production. They do not. `SPLIT_LEGEND` (`render.py:387-391` and its byte-identical
copy in `checks.py`) is printed on every one of the 3864 built pages and states a narrower rule
than the code applies.

This is squarely on the gate's own close criterion, judged verbatim: "the predicate is derived
from a published convention... and the page says what it was based on." The page's stated basis
is WRONG. A reader has no way to discover this without reading source -- which is exactly the
failure mode this whole run exists to close (a stated rule that does not match the applied rule).
It is not a corner case: it sits on the single sentence explaining the gate's central mechanism,
repeated on every page.

Confirmed no check pins the legend text to the predicate the way `RefsAccountingTests.
test_the_legend_names_the_predicates_the_count_actually_counts` pins `REFS_LEGEND` to
`load_stores`'s actual predicate set (grepped `tests/test_code_map.py` for `SPLIT_LEGEND`/
`top-level`/`top.level` -- the only three hits are the legend's own definition and the F5's own
render assertion that the legend text APPEARS on a page, never a check that its CONTENT matches
`is_test_module`'s real behavior). The gap the Commander named is real and unguarded.

RULING: BLOCKING. Two independently sufficient fixes, either closes it:
  (a) narrow the predicate to top-level-only (matches the implementer's OWN stated preference is
      the more permissive one -- see Assumptions section -- so this is the implementer choosing
      to keep the permissive reading, in which case (b) is the required fix instead), or
  (b) reword SPLIT_LEGEND to drop "top-level" (say "a tests package" or "a tests package anywhere
      on the module's dotted path").
Either way, ALSO add a check pinning the legend's claim to the real predicate (parallel to the
REFS_LEGEND precedent already in this file) so the two cannot drift silently again -- this is a
one-gate defect only if a regression guard closes it; otherwise it recurs at the next
`is_test_module` edit with nothing to catch it.

=== FINDING B: CONFIRMED as a real conflation; does NOT escape into anything shipped ===

Reproduced measure_split.py's exact headline numbers on a fresh build this run: unused 2428
(64.7%), test-only 451 (12.0%), production 873 (23.3%) of 3752 entity pages -- byte-for-byte match
to the IMPLEMENTER_RESULT's claim.

Wrote an independent re-measurement (`.agent-work/issue-456/evidence/g5_reviewer_split_by_definer.py`,
NOT imported from measure_split.py, built from scratch against the same fresh build) adding the
one dimension measure_split.py omits -- whether the entity's OWN module is itself a test module.
Cross-tab, exact match to the Commander's numbers:

  bucket       prod-defined   test-defined
  unused       88             2340
  test-only    2              449
  production   873            0

2340/2428 (96.4%) of "unused" is test-defined. Genuinely-unused production code is 88, a 27x
difference from the headline "2428." Separately verified TEST_NOTE's own distribution directly
(not inferred from the cross-tab): appears on exactly 2789 test-defined pages (= 2340+449+0,
consistent) and on 0 production-defined pages.

Checked whether the conflation escapes measure_split.py into anything SHIPPED, per the
Commander's explicit question. Read `render.top_index` and `render.module_index` in full and
grepped both files plus the rest of `scripts/` for `unused`/`test_only`/`test-only` -- zero hits
outside `checks.py`/`render.py`'s own split-grammar constants and `measure_split.py` itself.
Neither the top index nor any module index prints an aggregate unused/test-only/production count
anywhere in the rendered map tree. The three unrelated grep hits outside scripts/code_map (an
old superpowers spec doc, an unrelated HTML demo page, install_constellation.py) share no code
path with this gate and do not carry this claim.

RULING: NOT a shipped-artifact defect -- the per-page capability the gate's close criteria
actually require (a reader can tell the three states apart on ONE page) is real and independently
verified working. The defect is confined to the evidence layer: `measure_split.py` (committed as
this gate's own evidence script) and the IMPLEMENTER_RESULT's headline claim both reproduce the
exact conflation the gate exists to remove, in the ONE place a reader who trusts the aggregate
rather than a single page would be misled. Does not block the gate's shipped behavior by itself,
but the headline claim as currently phrased is actively wrong by 27x and must not propagate
further (e.g. into an epic-level summary or Triage) uncorrected -- flagged as a required fix, not
a blocker, since Finding A already blocks this gate on its own. Filed as a triage candidate for a
`measure_split.py` fix (add the definer dimension, or clearly re-scope the headline to "raw caller
counts, not adjusted for the entity's own definer" so it cannot be misread as a genuinely-unused
count).
